A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SNI research work. All pages, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, are readable and support comparison despite reorganized supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original PDE-solving experiments, prediction errors, data-efficiency studies and hyperparameter/data-augmentation ablations in Section 4 and Appendix A.7.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds nonlinear PDE results, additional geometries, architecture comparisons and runtime measurements in Appendices F and H.

M1.justification: The core domain decomposition and Schwarz iteration remain unchanged; Algorithm 1 chiefly clarifies existing inputs and rewrites the update equivalently. Appendix F.2 introduces an implemented acceleration variant that initializes SNI with direct GNOT predictions instead of the original zero interior solution.

E1.justification: v2 retains the four original PDE tasks and domains A–C, adds NonlinearLaplace2d with solution-dependent diffusivity, and evaluates Laplace2d-Dirichlet on dolphin-shaped and disk domains. These extend both equation coverage and geometric test conditions beyond v1.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained direct-GNOT baseline, v2 evaluates MeshGraphNets on Laplace2d domain A and compares SNI using Geo-FNO versus GNOT on two PDEs across A–C (Table 10). Appendix F also adds a classical FEM timing reference. Newly discussed methods such as CORAL and Transolver are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The original four tasks retain their documented data configurations, training settings and relative-l2 metric. v2 introduces a runtime protocol measuring convergence time and time to 15%, 10% and 5% error on one sample per equation/domain, plus a controlled initialization comparison. Table 6 also specifies the added nonlinear experiment's training, validation and testing configurations.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of local-operator architecture dependence, zero versus GNOT initialization, and spatial error localization alongside domain decomposition. These supplement the retained augmentation and partition/overlap/step-size analyses. The Darcy data-efficiency plots move from Figure 3 to Appendix Figure 8; they are not new analyses.

E5.justification: The existing reporting of means and standard deviations across random boundary/initial conditions, including 100-inference data-efficiency comparisons, is retained. No new training-seed repetition scheme, confidence intervals or formal significance-testing procedure is introduced; additional result rows do not establish a changed statistical practice.

E6.justification: New results include nonlinear SNI errors of 2.0–2.2% versus GNOT's 22–28% (Table 1), dolphin/disk errors of 4.5±0.9% and 2.1±0.5% (Table 9), architecture comparisons and runtime measurements. The new initialization experiment reports domain-A convergence times of 100 versus 28 seconds. The mixed-boundary GNOT error maps also change between v1 Figure 8 and v2 Figure 11.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 introduces explicit norm-contractivity and overlap assumptions and states both iterate and limiting-solution error bounds. Appendix C substantially rewrites v1's proof, replacing its random-fixed-point assertion with an error recurrence and Cauchy argument. The constant tau*t*c/(1-rho) already appeared in v1's proof. The revised convergence inference remains invalid because its residual 2c' need not vanish.

C1.justification: The central local-to-global framework, data-generation and SNI contributions remain. v2 withdraws the 'first attempt' novelty claim, explicitly extends its empirical claim to linear and nonlinear PDEs, and specifies elliptic assumptions for the theoretical guarantee.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive qualifications about unoptimized parallelization and lack of a speed advantage over FEM on the tested domains. It discusses runtime mechanisms, attributes architecture and dolphin-domain error gaps to generalization differences, and explains why extension to 3D requires additional research. Section 3.4 also distinguishes nonlinear empirical success from guaranteed convergence.

D1.justification: v1 promises post-review code release in its checklist; v2's abstract supplies a repository and declares public availability. v2 additionally documents original zero initialization, the GNOT initialization variant, incomplete parallelization, and nonlinear data-generation, training and normalization settings. Existing hardware and original-task implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning through a new complex-geometry discussion covering CORAL, Transolver and AROMA, plus additional domain-decomposition/PINN literature. It explicitly distinguishes its arbitrary-geometry objective from Mao et al.'s uniform-grid work and softens the earlier first-attempt claim. These are substantive additions beyond citation-format changes.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites affect the introduction, contribution bullets and inference explanation, including removal of the introductory generalizability ladder. Appendices A.1–A.8 become separately lettered sections, a reproducibility statement is added, and the NeurIPS checklist is removed. The main section sequence and much of the retained prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds runtime, initialization, geometry and architecture tables, plus basic-shape, decomposition, dolphin-domain, nonlinear-solution and error-localization figures. Existing tables gain rows/columns and percentage headings. Darcy data-efficiency panels are relocated and merged with appendix plots, mixed-boundary error panels are revised, and the document adopts ICLR formatting.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the added architecture and geometry tests, nonlinear results, code-access information and measured runtime limitations improve empirical support and transparency. The gain is limited by the unresolved convergence guarantee: Appendix C's nonvanishing 2c' bound does not establish a Cauchy sequence. Newly reported Geo-FNO scores also disagree between Section 4.3 and Table 10, reducing confidence in the expanded evidence.
